input.summary: 228 business functions mapped across 7 domains; only 6 active — 222 candidates await evidence closure to advance.
sources: Stakeholder interview evidence bundle (MER-SA07-INT-EVID-0001 through MER-SA07-INT-EVID-0033)
Core evidence refs MER-V3-EVID-0002 through MER-V3-EVID-0008

story.meaning: Meridian has broad functional coverage across 7 domains, but only 6 functions are active — the remaining 222 are stalled behind unresolved platform, governance, and data-foundation evidence gaps.
story.observed: 164 high-confidence and 64 medium-confidence function records are mapped. Every candidate use case — lakehouse, AI/LLM, cost transparency, payment integrity, call center — is blocked by the same upstream evidence deficits: no medallion architecture, no identity spine, no formal governance.
story.matters: Until evidence gates close, no function can advance from candidate to active, and no use case can reach decision grade. The breadth of the candidate pool signals strategic intent without execution readiness.
story.supports: CEO, CFO, CIO, CDAO, and Chief Experience Officer all cite overlapping priorities across these 7 domains, confirming cross-functional alignment — but alignment without evidence closure does not unlock investment.

findings: Only 6 of 228 functions are active (3%); 222 candidates are blocked — this is a governance and evidence-closure problem, not a strategy problem.

All five top use cases (lakehouse, AI/LLM, cost transparency, payment integrity, call center) share the same four upstream blockers: no medallion architecture, no identity spine, no formal governance, no certified semantic layer.

Seven distinct executive owners (CDAO, CMO, Health Plan COO, VP Quality, CFO, Chief Experience Officer, CDIO) are aligned on priorities but operating without a shared evidence-gate framework to sequence investment decisions.
Finance and Actuarial is the only domain with a high-confidence function still in candidate status — FP&A validation and benefits-ledger ties are the specific gate.

breakdown.title: Function Activation Status by Confidence Band

rows.label: Evidence Refs Loaded
rows.note: 89% evidence coverage; gaps are structural, not volumetric

chain: Business Functions → Use Cases (lakehouse, AI/LLM, cost transparency, payment integrity, call center)
Use Cases → Platform Evidence Gates (medallion architecture, identity spine, governance model, semantic layer)
Platform Evidence Gates → Executive Investment Decisions (CEO, CFO, CIO, CDAO, Chief Experience Officer)
Investment Decisions → Activation Status (candidate → active transition blocked until gates close)
relationships.note: All 7 domains feed into the same 5 priority use cases, and all 5 use cases share the same upstream platform evidence gaps — meaning a single governance and foundation evidence sprint unblocks the entire candidate portfolio simultaneously.

gaps.missing: No certified medallion architecture or patient/member identity spine
gaps.blocks: Unified clinical + claims lakehouse cannot advance; Clinical Operations and Health Plan Operations functions remain candidate
gaps.needed: Epic Clarity medallion build evidence + identity spine load confirmation
gaps.handoff: CDAO and CIO to certify architecture and identity evidence before next planning cycle

gaps.missing: No formal data governance operating model or certified semantic layer
gaps.blocks: All AI/LLM automation functions blocked; AI audit trail and data quality rules also absent
gaps.needed: Governance operating model charter + semantic layer ownership assignment + audit trail design
gaps.handoff: CDAO to own governance model; CISO to own AI audit trail evidence gate

gaps.missing: Provider contract terms not in governed digital form; attribution ownership unproven
gaps.blocks: End-to-end cost transparency and provider quality functions cannot reach decision grade
gaps.needed: Contract digitization project scoped; attribution model certified by Finance and Network Contracting
gaps.handoff: CFO and Health Plan COO to co-own contract digitization evidence closure

gaps.missing: Transcript governance, real-time CRM integration, and intent taxonomy uncertified
gaps.blocks: Call center optimization and Member Service Agent Assist functions stalled
gaps.needed: Transcript governance policy + Genesys/Salesforce real-time integration proof + intent taxonomy sign-off
gaps.handoff: Chief Experience Officer and Contact Center Ops to close transcript and taxonomy gates

gaps.missing: FP&A validation, benefits-ledger ties, and SAS model lineage ungoverned
gaps.blocks: Finance and Actuarial function activation and AI Benefits Realization Ledger use case
gaps.needed: FP&A usage extracts + benefits ledger framework + SAS lineage governance documentation
gaps.handoff: CFO to own benefits ledger; CDAO to govern SAS model lineage before payment integrity advances

evidence.name: Business Functions Master Dataset
evidence.facts: 164 high-confidence, 64 medium-confidence records across 7 domains and 7 executive owners; 89% evidence coverage by ref count
evidence.supports: Confirms functional breadth and activation gap; establishes domain-to-owner mapping
evidence.missing: Activation criteria thresholds not formalized; no evidence-gate SLA or sequencing framework documented

evidence.name: CEO / Enterprise Strategy Interview Bundle
evidence.type: Stakeholder interview evidence — synthetic planning grade
evidence.facts: CEO flags all 7 use cases as promising but not decision-grade; every item blocked by a distinct platform or data evidence gap
evidence.supports: Confirms executive intent and identifies specific evidence gates per use case
evidence.missing: No approved business case, baseline metrics, or PHI controls documented for any CEO-flagged use case

evidence.name: CFO / Finance & Value Interview Bundle
evidence.type: Stakeholder interview evidence — synthetic planning grade
evidence.rows: 7 context items across AI benefits ledger, cost transparency, payment integrity, automated close
evidence.facts: CFO prioritizes AI Benefits Realization Ledger and payment integrity; both blocked by FP&A validation and SAS lineage gaps
evidence.supports: Establishes Finance and Actuarial as the domain with highest executive urgency and most specific evidence requirements
evidence.missing: Budget, program, and benefits ledger ties not yet documented; FP&A usage extracts not provided

evidence.name: CIO / CISO / CTO Interview Bundle
evidence.type: Stakeholder interview evidence — synthetic planning grade
evidence.rows: 9 context items across platform, AI governance, spend governance
evidence.facts: CIO flags FY26 AI spend governance and unified lakehouse; CISO flags AI governance and model risk controls; CTO flags cost and payment integrity
evidence.supports: Confirms Technology Platform and Security domain activation is gated on AI audit trail and model risk evidence
evidence.missing: HITL controls, audit logging design, and model-risk evidence not yet loaded; AWS/Databricks foundation not certified

evidence.name: Contact Center and Member Experience Interview Bundle
evidence.type: Stakeholder interview evidence — synthetic planning grade
evidence.rows: 4 context items across agent assist, transcript governance, intent taxonomy
evidence.facts: Chief Experience Officer owns Member Service Agent Assist Transformation; blocked by transcript governance, real-time integration, and member identity linkage gaps
evidence.supports: Confirms Contact Center and Member Experience domain is activation-ready from a strategy standpoint but platform-blocked
evidence.missing: AHT, FCR, transfer rate, CSAT, and QA baselines not loaded; Genesys/Salesforce real-time integration not proven

evidence.name: Relationship and Risk Context Bundles
evidence.type: Cross-dimension gap registry — synthetic planning grade
evidence.rows: 298 relationship rows; 249 risk rows; 12 representative gap items
evidence.facts: 12 structural gaps repeat across all 5 top use cases; no gap is function-specific — all are shared platform and governance deficits
evidence.supports: Confirms that evidence closure is a platform-layer problem, not a domain-by-domain problem — a single foundation sprint unblocks the full candidate portfolio
evidence.missing: Gap remediation owners, timelines, and sequencing priorities not yet assigned across relationship and risk registries

data.annotation: All 222 candidate functions share ≤4 upstream blockers: medallion architecture, identity spine, governance model, semantic layer. Closing these gates simultaneously activates the full portfolio.
